findings.title: Do not mark failed work as complete
findings.body: The `finally` block completes the offset even when `result_processor` raises and the worker logs the failure. The commit loop can then advance past that result, preventing Kafka from redelivering it. The submission exception handler at lines 317–325 has the same problem: grouping or enqueue failures are marked complete even though the item was never processed. Only complete offsets after successful handling, or propagate failures for retry/DLQ processing.

findings.title: Do not shut down the factory-owned pool when a strategy closes
findings.body: The queue pool is created and retained by `ResultsStrategyFactory`, then shared with strategies created by that factory. Arroyo can close and recreate a strategy when partition assignments change; shutting down the shared pool here leaves the factory pointing at stopped workers or shut queues, so the replacement strategy cannot process messages. In this state submissions can remain unprocessed or fail and be acknowledged by the exception handler. Keep the pool alive until factory shutdown, or recreate it when the strategy is rebuilt.

findings.title: Use a shutdown mechanism supported by the project's Python versions
findings.body: `queue.Queue.shutdown()` was added in Python 3.13 and is unavailable on supported earlier Python versions. The resulting `AttributeError` is caught, but setting `worker.shutdown` does not wake workers blocked in `Queue.get()`. Each subsequent `join(timeout=5.0)` can time out; with the default 20 workers, normal shutdown can take about 100 seconds and leave daemon workers alive. Use a compatible wake-up mechanism, such as sentinels.

findings.title: Bound the work queues to provide backpressure
findings.body: A `Queue` with the default `maxsize=0` is unbounded, so `put()` never blocks when processing falls behind and the claimed natural backpressure does not occur. A sustained input rate above worker throughput will accumulate `WorkItem`s without limit and can exhaust process memory; each item also retains the original message payload. Set a finite queue capacity and define how the consumer handles a full queue.
